set.body:
Intaglio is correct and expressive but has no story for interactive-rate
redraw. Every consumer that resizes, hovers, brushes or scrubs a plot pays a
full pipeline run. This is now a blocking constraint for a downstream
interactive workspace (PLS Neuro spatial-response workspace, which needs
hover p95 <= 50 ms and cached plot update p95 <= 500 ms on faceted,
participant-level figures).

The library states the gap itself; this issue is to close it, not to
rediscover it.

## Evidence in-repo

- `docs/limits.md:171-172` -- "There is no streaming or incremental render
  path. A `Scene` is a fully materialized immutable tree, and
  `DeviceScene.fromScene` walks all of it."
- `docs/limits.md:173-174` -- "There is no caching of compiled plots.
  Compilation is pure ... but nothing memoizes it for you."
- `docs/design/interaction.md:253` -- "incremental scene updates, measured
  redraw budgets" sits in phase 6 of the interaction roadmap.
- `modules/interaction/README.md:85-87` -- "Picking is exhaustive and
  allocates geometry per target. No large-data capacity or latency guarantee
  is established by these queries. Spatial indexing and incremental updates
  remain separate work."
- `performance/README.md:2-5` -- the performance gate "deliberately does not
  fail CI on elapsed time".

## The structural problem

`PlotCompiler` runs one undifferentiated pipeline (`PlotCompiler.scala:428-460`;
faceted: `FacetCompiler.scala:34-115`):

    mapping -> stats -> scale training -> row resolution -> coord
            -> layout solve -> geom lowering -> guide lowering -> device lowering

Only the last four phases depend on the device. `PlotCompiler.resolve` merely
sets `options.renderContext` (`PlotCompiler.scala:398-402`) and
`effectiveOptions` rebuilds the whole `LayoutPolicy` from it
(`PlotCompiler.scala:404-426`). So a pure resize -- where not one datum
changed -- recomputes histogram bins, density kernels, summary intervals and
scale domains.

That seam is the fix. Split the pipeline at the data/device boundary and the
common interactive cases become cheap without any new caching policy.

## Faceting multiplies it

- `FacetCompiler.scala:114-121` runs `MappingPhase.planPanels` then
  `StatPhase.transform` per panel, then `resolveLayers` per panel, *plus* one
  global pass for shared scale training (`FacetCompiler.scala:39-52`) --
  roughly (panels + 1) full stat/resolve passes.
- `facetGrid` materializes the full row x column cross product
  (`Facet.scala:139-148` vs `:188-194`), so empty cells still cost a pass.
- Free scales lower per-panel axes individually and measure each panel's tick
  labels (`FacetCompiler.scala:220-256`, `:341-352`).
- `PlotBuilder.resolve` defaults to `rich` (= `Full` provenance) while
  `PlotCompiler.compile` defaults to `lean` (`docs/limits.md:133-134`,
  `PlotCompiler.scala:80-90`), so a DSL-built faceted plot retains one
  `ResolvedRow` per datum per panel and forfeits the point-batch IR
  (`docs/limits.md:91-94`).

A 30-panel x 20-subject figure -- an ordinary neuroimaging trellis -- is
therefore ~31 full stat+resolve passes, repeated on every resize, with
per-datum provenance retained.

## No cost model exists for any of this

`performance/baselines/v1.tsv` (reproduced `docs/limits.md:29-51`) records
cardinality, not time, across six workloads (`docs/limits.md:64-71`): 20k
scatter, 256x256 raster, 10k dodge, 10k stack, 8192-level discrete lookup,
50k histogram, 10k-mark SVG. **None is faceted.** A grep of
`modules/performance/**` finds no facet workload. There is consequently no
answer to "what does a 30-panel plot cost", and no regression signal if it
gets worse.

## What "fast" should mean here

Proposed acceptance targets, to be refined once measurement exists:

1. A resize that changes only `RenderContext` does no statistical work and no
   scale retraining.
2. A hover/pick query on a faceted plot is sublinear in mark count.
3. A faceted compile is not asymptotically worse per panel than an equivalent
   standalone plot, and empty `facetGrid` cells cost nothing.
4. The performance baseline includes at least one many-panel workload and one
   resize-only workload, and reports elapsed time even if CI does not gate on
   it.

Children track the separable pieces. Numbers above are read from source and
docs, not measured; the first child to land should be the measurement one so
the rest are judged against real figures rather than these estimates.
set.title: Interactive-rate rendering: incremental redraw, compile memoization and a published cost model
